slides.title: You don't even enjoy p*rn anymore. [[So why can't you stop?]]
slides.sub: The difference between wanting and liking.

slides.title: Wanting ≠ [[liking]]
slides.body: Brain researchers separate wanting something from enjoying it. With p*rn addiction, the wanting can stay loud long after the enjoyment fades.

slides.title: The [[chase]]
slides.body: Searching, scrolling, clicking — the hunt for the "right" p*rn video often feels bigger than the video itself. You're hooked on the chase.

slides.title: Empty [[after]]
slides.body: Many people describe feeling flat or numb after p*rn — not satisfied. That gap between craving and reward is a sign p*rn has become a compulsion.

slides.title: Use the [[gap]]
items: Write down how p*rn actually makes you feel.
Read it when the next urge hits.
Let the craving pass — it always does.
slides.note: Do you feel worse or better after p*rn? Comment WORSE or BETTER 👇

carousels.name: P*rn addiction is wrecking your sleep

slides.title: Late-night p*rn is [[stealing your sleep.]]
slides.sub: And bad sleep makes the next p*rn urge even stronger.

slides.title: The [[late]] start
slides.body: "Just one video" at midnight becomes p*rn until 2 AM. That's hours of sleep gone — night after night.

slides.title: Tired brain, [[weak]] brakes
slides.body: Sleep-deprived people tend to make more impulsive choices. So a bad night after p*rn sets up an even harder night tomorrow.

slides.title: The sleep–p*rn [[loop]]
slides.body: Break it at the start: protect your bedtime.

carousels.name: How to tell your partner about your p*rn addiction

slides.title: How to tell your partner about your [[p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: What to say — and what not to say.

slides.title: Pick the [[right]] moment
slides.body: Not in the middle of a fight. Not over text. A calm, private time when you can both talk about p*rn honestly.

slides.title: Lead with [[honesty]]
slides.body: "I've been struggling with p*rn and I want to be honest with you." Don't minimize it. Don't blame them.

slides.title: Expect [[emotion]]
slides.body: They may feel hurt, angry or confused. That's normal. Listen first. Their feelings about your p*rn use are valid.

slides.title: Come with a [[plan]]
items: Explain what you're doing to quit p*rn.
slides.note: Partners and quitters: what helped this conversation go well? 👇

slides.title: 30+, married, good job. [[Still addicted to p*rn.]]
slides.sub: You're not the only one — and it's not too late.

slides.title: It doesn't [[age out]]
slides.body: Many men thought p*rn was a phase they'd grow out of. For plenty, p*rn addiction just got better at hiding behind a busy life.

slides.title: More to [[lose]] now
slides.body: A partner, kids, a career, your own self-respect. The cost of p*rn addiction gets heavier as life gets fuller.

slides.title: Decades of [[habit]]
slides.body: 15–20 years of p*rn doesn't undo in a week. Be patient with yourself. But change at any age is possible.

slides.title: Where to [[start]]
items: Admit it to yourself — that's step one.
Block p*rn on every device, including work.
Find support: a therapist, a group, an app.
slides.note: Over 30 and quitting p*rn? Say "me too" — you're not alone 👇

slides.title: Quitting p*rn today? [[Do these 5 things first.]]
Block p*rn [[everywhere]]
slides.body: Phone, laptop, tablet. Not "later" — today. Removing easy access to p*rn is the single biggest early win.

slides.title: Write your [[why]]
slides.body: One sentence: why you're quitting p*rn. Put it somewhere you'll see it every single day.

slides.title: Know your [[triggers]]
slides.body: When do you usually watch p*rn? Late nights? Bored? Stressed? List your top 3. Those are your danger zones.

slides.title: Steps [[4–5]]
items: Plan your urge response: leave the room, move, breathe.
Track every day — progress you can see keeps you going.
